subject: history_social
passage: Rani Pokhari, a large rectangular pond in the center of Kathmandu, Nepal, was built in 1670 on the orders of King Pratap Malla. According to tradition, the king had the pond dug to console his queen after the death of one of their sons, and a small temple was raised on an island at its ______ the pond was badly damaged in the earthquake of 2015, its restoration became a subject of public debate, with many residents insisting that the walls be rebuilt in traditional brick and lime mortar rather than concrete. The restored pond reopened in 2020.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "According to tradition, the king had the pond dug … and a small temple was raised on an island at its center" is a complete sentence. "When the pond was badly damaged in the earthquake of 2015, its restoration became a subject of public debate" is another complete sentence, made of a "When" clause followed by its main clause. Two complete sentences need a period (or equivalent) between them.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The period is right, but no comma may separate the subordinating word "When" from the clause it introduces.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma alone cannot join the sentence ending at "center" to the sentence that begins with the "when" clause; this is a comma splice.
explanation.C: Correct. The period ends the first sentence, and "When" begins a new sentence whose main clause is "its restoration became a subject of public debate."
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the two sentences run together, and the reader cannot tell where the first one ends.
